_comment: VideoSegmenter backend settings. Precedence: environment variable > this file > built-in defaults. Relative paths for temp_dir/projects_dir/log_dir resolve against the process working directory; relative model paths (sam3.checkpoint, sam3.bpe_path) resolve against the backend folder. Point VSR_CONFIG_FILE at another file to use it instead of this one.

sessions._comment: A session is the frame working copy of one open project. ttl_seconds is how long an idle one survives; max_bytes is the disk backstop across every client, and max_bytes_per_client is a single client's share, so one reviewer's large project cannot evict another reviewer's open clip.

sam3._comment: Set enabled=false to run the backend without SAM 3 at all: no model is probed or loaded and /api/sam3 and /api/propagate answer 503. `checkpoint` points at a local sam3.pt (relative paths resolve against backend/); leave it null to download the gated facebook/sam3 weights instead, which needs `hf auth login`. `bpe_path` can stay null: the tokenizer vocabulary ships inside the sam3 package. `eager` loads the models while the server starts and keeps them resident; `max_resident_models` is how many fit at once (2 = the image model and the video predictor together, so neither load evicts the other). `image_cache_size` is how many frames keep their vision embeddings for click-by-click prompting per reviewer, and `image_cache_clients` how many reviewers keep such a cache: the budget is per client, so one reviewer's clicks cannot evict another's frames. 1 reproduces a single shared cache; raising the client count multiplies peak host memory by the same factor.

propagate._comment: window_frames is how many frames one SAM 3 session holds while propagating and overlap is how many neighboring windows share (the re-anchoring stretch). A longer range is split into overlapping windows, so a mask can be propagated to the end of any clip; there is no frame cap. chaining decides what a window with no hand-verified mask may be seeded with: 'derived' (default) hands it the previous window's own prediction, which is what reaches the whole clip; 'verified' stops the run instead, so it never travels more than one window past a mask a human drew. A request may override it per run. max_jobs is the queue ceiling across every client and max_jobs_per_client is one reviewer's share of it, so a single client cannot fill the queue and stop everyone else starting a run.
